subject: MSA + Order Form — Clarify output & training permissions / redline next steps
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Cho <mike.cho@skyline.com>, contracts@skyline.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Skyline redlines: output ownership + training permission questions

Jonas — thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redlined MSA + order form (see embedded change highlights). A couple of items we need clarity on before legal can sign: 

1) Output ownership: your standard Order Form states Customer gets "all outputs", but our legal team is asking for an explicit carveout for Redwood-generated model improvements and any aggregated telemetry. We want to ensure Skyline can use outputs in our product, but not grant Redwood rights to retrain public models on our outputs. 

2) Training / feedback license: the redline proposes a mandatory, perpetual feedback/training license from Skyline to Redwood. We need options: either (a) one-way telemetry with opt-out for any data used for model training, or (b) a narrow, time-limited license tied to improving the hosted service only. 

3) Attribution & derivative claims: are there guardrails Redwood can propose that limit derivative claims on Skyline product features that merely surface generated text?

Can you loop in whoever manages order-form-level IP language on your side? We highlighted specific lines in the attached doc. Would like to get to a mutual position by end of week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product
Skyline Analytics

Attachments: Skyline_OrderForm_v2.docx (redlines), redlines_summary.xlsx (highlights)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline redlines: output ownership + training permission questions

Elena — thanks for sending this through and for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (product/legal interface) and Laura (legal) to propose legally vetted options. High-level response before they chime in: 

- We do not assert ownership over customer outputs; our default language is to grant customers broad usage rights in their downstream products. That said, we can propose a narrow carveout where Redwood retains rights to aggregated, anonymized telemetry used for model quality improvements (not customer-identifiable outputs).

- For the feedback/training license: we can offer a toggleable option on the Order Form: 
  * Standard: non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual feedback license (enables continuous hosted improvements).
  * Opt-in limited: a 12-month, non-exclusive license limited to service improvement only, with a telemetry-only data pipeline (no raw customer output persisted).

- Attribution/derivative claims: we can propose explicit language that customer product features that rely on or surface model outputs (without taking Redwood's model weights) are not treated as Redwood derivative works.

Karthik/Laura — please see Elena's redlines and suggest precise replacement clauses (redline-friendly) plus a short rationale for each option. Elena — we'll try to aim for a single-track recommendation so we don't leave procurement juggling multiple counteroffers.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: consent_options.pdf (draft consent toggle options)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline redlines: output ownership + training permission questions

Quick internal note and proposal copy for Laura to transform into legal text.

Proposal summary (for contract line edits):
1) Output ownership: Replace ambiguous "All outputs" sentence in Order Form with: 
   "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Outputs, subject to the limited rights expressly granted to Provider in Section X (Aggregated Telemetry)."
   Rationale: preserves customer usage while allowing Redwood to operate and improve service using only aggregated signals.

2) Aggregated Telemetry carveout (new Section X): 
   "Provider may collect, aggregate and use non-identifiable metadata and usage signals derived from Customer's use of the Service ("Aggregated Telemetry") for purposes of service operation, analytics and model quality improvements, provided that such Aggregated Telemetry does not include Customer Outputs or any Customer Data elements in raw form."
   Rationale: narrow, allows Redwood to continuously improve without exposing outputs.

3) Feedback / Training license — two paths (Order Form checkbox selects one):
   Option A (Hosted continuous improvement - Standard): Non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use Customer Feedback and Aggregated Telemetry to train Provider models for service improvements.
   Option B (Limited opt-in): time-bound (12 months), limited to anonymized telemetry only, revocable at contract renewal; Provider will not persist raw Customer Outputs for training.

4) Attribution / Derivative limitation: Add carveout language clarifying that Provider's underlying models and weights remain Provider IP and Customer productizations that merely surface generated outputs are not automatically treated as derivative model works.

Laura — can you draft clean redline text for each item above and include a short cover note that procurement can share with Skyline legal. Also call out any downstream compliance or SOC2 implications (telemetry retention windows, ability to opt-out).

Karthik
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 May 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline redlines: output ownership + training permission questions

Elena — attached are two items: (1) a redline PDF that replaces the ambiguous "outputs" language and inserts the Aggregated Telemetry section; (2) a short table that summarizes the two feedback license options and recommended default. Highlights: 

- We recommend offering Option B (12-month, anonymized telemetry, revocable) to mid-market customers as a default for new orders; Option A remains available for enterprise with a commercial concession. Rationale: reduces procurement friction while preserving a path for customers that want continuous hosted improvements.

- Tech/ops note: if Skyline picks Option B, we will configure the onboarding to enable telemetry-only pipelines and a 30-day retention window for raw logs; only aggregated signals are stored longer term. We will log this in the order form via a selected checkbox and a short table showing retention windows.

- Doc language included: the redline uses simple, contract-safe phrasing; I kept the Aggregated Telemetry definition tight to avoid scope creep. If Skyline wants a carveout allowing Redwood to keep model improvements that are directly trained on anonymized customer interactions, we can make that explicit in the enterprise section (with compensation).

Next steps: 
  1) Elena/procurement — please confirm whether Skyline prefers Option A or B (or needs a variant).
  2) If Option A chosen, provide the person who can authorize commercial concession (we'll need to loop Revenue/Sales Ops).
  3) If Option B, confirm any specific retention windows (default 30 days) and we'll update the order form checkbox text.

I'll send clean PDF redlines and an editable doc for your counsel.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Skyline_OrderForm_v2_LR_redline.pdf, consent_options.pdf
